- Small, discrete, dark/black raised dots scattered across a green leaf surface
- Larger, elongated dark lesions concentrated along the midrib area
- Slight brownish discoloration around some spots
- No powdery coatings or pustules

Top candidates: **Tar_spot** (black raised stromata on green leaf) and **Physoderma_brown_spot** (dark midrib lesions + leaf stippling). Let me compare references.
The Tar_spot reference closely matches — small black raised dots on green leaf. The Physoderma_brown_spot shows more yellow stippling. Let me check a few more candidates to confirm.
Common rust shows orange-brown pustules; Holcus_spot shows tan-centered lesions — both clearly different. Let me check two more to meet the 6-view minimum.

Southern rust shows bright orange clustered pustules; Eyespot shows yellow-orange ringed circular lesions — both completely different from the test image.

**Analysis Summary:**

The test image shows a corn leaf with:
- **Small, discrete black raised/glossy dots** scattered across a green leaf blade — exactly the "raised black stromata" of Tar_spot
- **Dark elongated lesions along the midrib** with a yellowish-white midrib band — matches Tar_spot's description of dark lesions running parallel to veins with midrib involvement
- Leaf tissue remains mostly green (early-moderate infection)

All other candidates are eliminated:
- Rusts (Common, Southern): orange/brick-red pustules — absent here
- Physoderma_brown_spot: requires yellow stippling across blade — not present; midrib dark spots alone don't fit
- Holcus_spot: tan/white centered round spots with brown borders — not black raised stromata
- Eyespot: yellow-orange ringed circular lesions — clearly different

The black glossy raised stromata scattered on a green leaf with midrib dark lesions is the diagnostic signature of **Tar_spot**.
